modules.brief: Read, write, edit and list the files of the workspace.
modules.detail:
Reading is the cheap direction of this sandbox and writing is the expensive one, so a program that reads a dozen files to decide what to change is well shaped, while one that rewrites forty large files in a single turn will exhaust its fuel budget.

Nothing here places anything in the context window. `Views.openFile` is the call that does.

modules.brief: Run shell commands in the workspace.
modules.detail: One call, and the way a program reaches everything gg has no tool for: a build, a test run, `git`, `curl`, a package manager. The workspace is the working directory.

modules.brief: The epic and issue board, on which work is decomposed into dispatchable units.
modules.detail: An issue is heavyweight and self-contained: it says what is in scope, what is not, and how it will be judged done, and gg dispatches it to the agent it names. That is what makes it different from a task, which is a note an agent keeps for itself.

modules.brief: A private task list, held as a graph with blocker edges.
modules.detail: Small units of one agent's own work. Nobody dispatches from it — the board is where other agents pick work up — and a task blocked on others becomes actionable when the last of them is done.

modules.brief: Durable memories, which survive a context compaction.
modules.detail:
A run picks one of three memory strategies and binds only that strategy's calls: the scratchpad's `writeMemory` and `updateMemory`, or the file-shaped `createMemory`, `readMemory` and `editMemory` — plus `searchMemories` where there is no pinned index. `deleteMemory` is bound under all three, the system prompt says which strategy is in force, and `list` is the directory of what was really bound.

A memory may carry code, which is a module in this language bound at `lib.<name>` in every later program — a helper written once. It costs no context window and is never shown back.

modules.brief: Put a file, a computed value or a function's documentation into the context window.
modules.detail:
A program's own output goes nowhere the model can read it. A view is how a program puts something in front of the model that wrote it: one attributable item in the next prompt, closeable once it has been read.

There are three kinds and the list is closed: a file, a computed string, and one function's documentation. A picture is not a fourth kind — it is a file view of an image file, and the view carries the picture.

modules.brief: Reclaim room in the agent's own context window.
modules.detail:
Four calls, in the order a full window wants them: drop file views that are done with, move whole turns into the archive, search the archive for what was moved, and — when none of that is enough — compact.

These are the only calls whose effect is on the conversation rather than on the workspace, and they are worth making from a program precisely because a program can decide when: read a set of files, extract what matters, and evict the views in the same turn.

modules.brief: Delegate work to child agents, and hand this session on to another agent.
modules.detail:
A child runs in parallel with its own window and its own model. It sees the brief it was given and nothing of the conversation that produced it, so a brief has to be self-contained — which is also why an issue, whose scope is written down, briefs a child better than a sentence does.

Waiting can dominate a turn's wall clock, because it blocks while real agents run and the run's budget keeps ticking. Spawning broadly and waiting once beats spawning and waiting in a loop.

modules.brief: Read the authored skills this run offers.
modules.detail: A skill is a procedure somebody wrote down. The ones a run offers are named in the system prompt, and reading one pins it into the session permanently.

modules.brief: Fetch a program this session already ran, and hand a patched copy back to be run.
modules.detail:
Under responses as code a reply is a whole program, so a one-character mistake in a sixty-line program costs the sixty lines again. The library makes the fix proportional to the mistake: fetch what ran, patch it with ordinary string work, hand it back.

```java
Programs.rerun(Programs.get().replace("Files.readfile", "Files.readFile"));
```

modules.brief: End the session, with the ending the agent's role has.
modules.detail:
Under responses as code every reply is a program, so there is no prose turn that could mean "the work is done" — a model that answers "task complete" has written a reply that failed to be a program rather than an ending. These are the calls that mean it, and which of them a program has is decided by the role the agent was dispatched in: an agent doing work ends with `Session.finish`, and a reviewer with `Session.approve` or `Session.requestChanges`.

None of them stops the program. Whatever follows still runs, which is why they belong last, and a program that then fails cancels its own ending and gets another turn.

modules.brief: The types every other module's signatures name, and the exception every gg call throws.
modules.detail: It is the one module with no class of its own, because none of it is a call: a failure, the classes of failure, and the shape of a module's own directory. Everything here is in scope in every program without qualification.

functions.name: shell
functions.brief: Run a command with `sh -c` in the workspace and hand back what it printed.
functions.detail:
A non-zero exit is not a failure: it arrives as `exitCode` on the result. Only a process that could not be launched, or one the timeout killed, throws.

This run may offload shell output, and the `shell` tool's own description says which mode is in force. Under `offload`, `output` holds the tail that fits and ends with a note naming the two files the whole of stdout and stderr went to. Under `adaptive`, the default, a command that succeeded returns only that note and one that failed returns the tail. Grepping the named files beats running the command again.

Returns: what the command printed, and how it exited

Throws `ToolError`: `ToolErrorCode.LIMIT_EXCEEDED` when the timeout killed the process, and `ToolErrorCode.IO_ERROR` when it could not be launched.

`shell(String command, int timeoutSecs)` — Run a command with a deadline of the program's own rather than gg's default of 120 seconds.

parameters.doc: The command line, run by `sh -c` with the workspace as its working directory.

parameters.doc: The command line, run by `sh -c` with the workspace as its working directory.

parameters.name: timeoutSecs
parameters.doc: How long to let it run before killing it, in seconds. It is clamped to whatever is left of the run's wall-clock budget.

functions.name: waitForIssue
functions.brief: Register a wait on an issue, which suspends the session between turns rather than now.
functions.detail:
It records the wait and returns at once, so the rest of the program still runs. Once the program ends the run suspends, freeing this agent's slot for others, until the issue is terminal — done, or failed if its assigned agent could not complete it — and then resumes on the next turn. It is how the next turn's work is sequenced behind an issue this one depends on.

Returns: gg's acknowledgement that the wait is registered

functions.name: openFile
functions.brief: Read a file and show it in the context window, keyed by its path.
functions.detail:
The split from `Files.readFile` is the point: that call gets bytes for the program and this one puts the file in front of the model, so a program that reads forty files to grep them costs nothing. An image file is shown as a picture, and this is the only way to look at one.

Re-opening a file already open replaces what it showed rather than piling up a duplicate, so a program may open the same file every turn without the window growing.

Returns: the file's text, or the picture's description

Throws `ToolError`: `ToolErrorCode.NOT_FOUND` for a missing path. The read is what fails, and nothing is opened when it does.

`openFile(String path, int offset, int limit)` — Show one page of a file rather than the whole of it.

Two pages of one file are two views that coexist; re-opening the same page replaces what it showed rather than piling up a duplicate.

Returns: the window of the file's text, or the picture's description

Throws `ToolError`: `ToolErrorCode.NOT_FOUND` for a missing path, and `ToolErrorCode.INVALID_ARGUMENT` for an offset past the end of the file.

parameters.name: path
parameters.doc: The file to open, relative to the workspace or absolute.

parameters.name: limit

functions.name: openText
functions.brief: Show a value the program computed, under a label.
functions.detail:
A directory listing, a command's output, a child agent's answer, a table the program assembled. Opening the same label again replaces what it showed, so a program may refine one view in a loop without piling up a copy per iteration.

Throws `ToolError`: `ToolErrorCode.INVALID_ARGUMENT` for an empty label — a view with no selector could never be closed or attributed — and `ToolErrorCode.LIMIT_EXCEEDED`, naming the cap, for a body or label over gg's caps. Nothing is silently truncated.

parameters.name: label
parameters.doc: What to file the view under. It is what `close` takes, and opening the same label again replaces what it showed. It may not be empty.

parameters.name: body
parameters.doc: What to show. An empty body is allowed: it is how a program says that something it was showing is now empty.

functions.name: openDocsView
functions.brief: Show the full documentation for one function: its signature, its description, and its types.
functions.detail:
This is how a function is read. It is a view rather than a return value — the documentation arrives in the next prompt under a `Documentation` heading keyed by the name, exactly as a file or a computed value arrives — so it is not available in the turn that asks for it. Ask in one turn, use it in the next. Opening the same function's documentation again replaces the view rather than adding a second copy, and `close` closes it.

Throws `ToolError`: `ToolErrorCode.NOT_FOUND` for an unknown or unbound name.

parameters.name: name
parameters.doc: The function to document, by the name it is called by — `"readFile"` for `Files.readFile`. Each module's `list` is what says which names exist.

functions.name: close
functions.brief: Close every view carrying a selector, freeing the tokens they occupied.
functions.detail:
For a file that is every page of that path, for a text view the one with that label, for a documentation view the function's name. Closing a selector that is not open hands back `0` rather than failing, so a program that tidies up unconditionally needs no guard. Closing a file view forgets what was read rather than what exists; closing a text view discards the only copy of what it held.

Returns: how many views were closed

parameters.name: selector
parameters.doc: What the view is filed under: a file's path, a text view's label, or a documentation view's function name.

functions.name: current
functions.brief: List what is open in the context window right now, with what each costs.
functions.detail:
Each entry carries its kind, the selector that closes it, roughly what it costs in tokens, and — for a paged file view — the region it covers. It is called `current` rather than `list` because every module already carries a `list` of its own functions.

Returns: every view open in the context window

functions.name: close
functions.brief: Close this view, which is `Views.close` on its own selector.
functions.detail: Returns: how many views were closed, which is one unless it had already gone

functions.name: evictFileView
functions.brief: Drop what one file, or every file, put in the context window, and report what that freed.
functions.detail:
Called with nothing it drops every file read into the window. The files on disk are untouched either way: this forgets what was read rather than what exists.

Returns: what the eviction reclaimed

`evictFileView(String path)` — Drop the contents of one file read into the context window.

parameters.name: path
parameters.doc: The file whose views to drop.

functions.name: archiveThread
functions.brief: Move whole turns out of the context window, and report what that freed.
functions.detail:
Every result carries a header with its turn number and roughly what holding it costs, which is what the spans are named from: a span is inclusive at both ends, so `new Context.TurnRange(4, 19)` archives turns 4 through 19. An archived turn's own messages are dropped; its results are kept and stay searchable with `searchArchive`.

Returns: what the archive reclaimed

Throws `ToolError`: `ToolErrorCode.INVALID_ARGUMENT` for a span whose ends are not turn numbers.

parameters.name: ranges
parameters.doc: The inclusive spans of turn numbers to move out of the window.

functions.name: searchArchive
functions.brief: Search archived history for a case-insensitive substring, most recent first, up to eight hits.
functions.detail:
`archiveEmpty` is worth reading before `hits`: it tells "nothing has been archived yet" apart from "the search ran and matched nothing", so a program does not archive again believing the first archive failed.

Returns: what the search found, and whether there was anything to search

parameters.name: query
parameters.doc: The substring to look for. Matching is case-insensitive.

functions.name: compact
functions.brief: Compact the context window: the detailed thread is dropped and restarted from a summary.
functions.detail:
Skills, memories and the task list are kept as they are, and each named file is read afresh. gg asks for this call when the window is full, and refuses every other call until it arrives.

It does not stop the program: it registers the request and returns, and the rewrite happens once the program has ended. Everything not in the summary and not re-read is gone, so the summary is written for the agent that wakes up next.

Throws `ToolError`: `ToolErrorCode.REFUSED` when a compaction is already in flight and this call is not the one it asked for.

parameters.name: summary
parameters.doc: What the restarted window opens with. Everything not in it and not re-read from `files` is gone.

parameters.name: files
parameters.doc: The paths to read afresh into the restarted window. Naming none reads nothing back.

functions.name: spawnSubagent
functions.brief: Delegate scoped work to a child agent, and hand back its handle immediately.
functions.detail:
The child runs in parallel while this program continues. The agent named selects the child's model, tools and instructions, and must be one this agent may spawn; the brief is either self-contained instructions or the id of a board issue. The child shares the workspace.

Returns: the child's handle, to wait on or to message

Throws `ToolError`: `ToolErrorCode.LIMIT_EXCEEDED` at the delegation depth cap, and `ToolErrorCode.INVALID_ARGUMENT` when `agent` is not one this agent may spawn.

parameters.name: agent
parameters.doc: The agent profile to run the child as, from the ones this agent may spawn.

parameters.name: brief
parameters.doc: What the child is to do: `Delegation.Brief.prompt` with self-contained instructions, or `Delegation.Brief.issue` with a board issue's id.

functions.name: waitForSubagents
functions.brief: Block until the named children have finished, and collect their results in dispatch order.
functions.detail:
Naming none waits for every child still outstanding, which is the shape worth reaching for: the run's wall-clock budget keeps running while a program waits, so one wait for many children costs far less than one wait per child.

Returns: every collected child's result, in dispatch order

Throws `ToolError`: `ToolErrorCode.NOT_FOUND` for an unknown id.

parameters.name: ids
parameters.doc: The children to wait for, as `spawnSubagent` returned them. Naming none waits for every one still outstanding.

functions.name: sendMessage
functions.brief: Deliver a message to a running child agent's inbox, which it reads at its next turn.
functions.detail: Throws `ToolError`: `ToolErrorCode.NOT_FOUND` for an unknown agent id, and `ToolErrorCode.CONFLICT` when that child has already returned.

parameters.name: agentId
parameters.doc: The child to deliver to, as `spawnSubagent` returned it.

parameters.name: message
parameters.doc: What to put in its inbox.

functions.name: transitionState
functions.brief: Move the process this agent is running inside on to another of its states.
functions.detail:
Bound only while a state machine is driving the session and the current state has somewhere to go. Like a compaction it is registered rather than performed: the call validates the target and returns, the program runs on to its end, and the transition happens after that — replacing the agent, and its window, mid-program would pull every remaining call out from under it. The first declaration in a turn stands.

Throws `ToolError`: `ToolErrorCode.INVALID_ARGUMENT` for a state this agent may not move to, and `ToolErrorCode.REFUSED` for a second declaration in one turn.

`transitionState(String state, String note)` — Move on to another state, telling the agent that takes over something as it starts.

parameters.name: state
parameters.doc: The state to move on to, named the way an agent to spawn is named.

parameters.name: state
parameters.doc: The state to move on to, named the way an agent to spawn is named.

parameters.name: note
parameters.doc: The opening message the next state's agent sees.

functions.name: exec
functions.brief: Continue this session as a different agent, from the next turn.
functions.detail:
The named agent takes over with its own model, tools and instructions, keeping every capability the two of them share — the whole conversation above all, so it needs no catching up. Registered rather than performed, exactly as a state transition is and for the same reason. A session makes one succession per turn, and this is bound only where the agent may make transitions, has agents it may become, and is not being driven by a state machine.

Throws `ToolError`: `ToolErrorCode.INVALID_ARGUMENT` for an agent this one may not become, and `ToolErrorCode.REFUSED` for a second succession in one turn.

`exec(String agent, String prompt)` — Continue this session as a different agent, telling it what to do as it takes over.

parameters.name: agent
parameters.doc: The agent to become, from the ones this agent may become.

parameters.name: agent
parameters.doc: The agent to become, from the ones this agent may become.

parameters.name: prompt
parameters.doc: Its opening message. It already has the whole conversation, so this is the instruction rather than a briefing.

functions.name: fork
functions.brief: Run a copy of this agent, in parallel, on something it will not do itself.
functions.detail:
The copy has the same model, the same tools and a private copy of the whole conversation, so the prompt is the difference rather than a briefing. Its handle comes back immediately, but the copy starts once this turn's results are recorded — the conversation it inherits has to be a complete one — so it can only be collected on a later turn.

Returns: the copy's handle, to collect on a later turn

Throws `ToolError`: `ToolErrorCode.LIMIT_EXCEEDED` at the delegation depth cap.

parameters.name: prompt
parameters.doc: What the copy is to do instead. It has the whole conversation already, so this is the difference rather than a briefing.

functions.name: send
functions.brief: Deliver a message to this child, which is `Delegation.sendMessage` on its own id.
functions.detail: Throws `ToolError`: `ToolErrorCode.CONFLICT` when the child has already returned.

parameters.name: message
parameters.doc: What to put in its inbox. It reads it at its next turn.

functions.name: readSkill
functions.brief: Read an authored skill by name, its front matter stripped.
functions.detail:
The skill is also pinned permanently into the session's context, so it survives a compaction and never has to be read twice. A skill that carries code binds that code at `lib.<name>` for every later program, and a skill that carries an on-use script has it run once the program ends, with whatever it shows arriving on the next turn.

Returns: the skill's body, with its front matter stripped

Throws `ToolError`: `ToolErrorCode.NOT_FOUND`, listing the skills this run does have, for a name none of them has.

parameters.name: name
parameters.doc: The skill's name, exactly as the system prompt lists it.

functions.name: history
functions.brief: Every program this session has run, oldest first.
functions.detail:
It lists shapes rather than sources, so a directory of forty programs costs a few lines each. The list survives a compaction, which makes it the way back to a program whose text has left the context window. A session that has run nothing yet gets an empty list rather than a failure.

Returns: every program this session has run, oldest first

functions.name: get
functions.brief: The exact source of one program this session ran, as a string; with no turn, the most recent.
functions.detail:
The first half of fixing a program without rewriting it: get what ran, patch it with ordinary string work, hand the result to `rerun`. What comes back is the program that executed — so where a turn's program was itself handed over by `rerun`, this is the program that ran rather than the few lines that asked for it, and fetch-patch-run composes turn after turn.

Returns: the source of the last program this session ran

Throws `ToolError`: `ToolErrorCode.NOT_FOUND`, naming the turns that are held, when nothing has run yet.

`get(int turn)` — The program that ran on one particular turn, rather than the most recent one.

Returns: the source of the program that ran on that turn

Throws `ToolError`: `ToolErrorCode.NOT_FOUND`, naming the turns that are held, for a turn that ran no program or one old enough that the library has dropped it.

parameters.name: turn
parameters.doc: The turn whose program to fetch, as `history` reports it.

functions.name: rerun
functions.brief: Hand gg a program to run in place of this one.
functions.detail:
This program finishes, then gg compiles and runs `source` as the turn's program. Nothing is undone: every call already made stands, and the program that runs next sees the world this one left behind — so a hand-over belongs before work that should not happen twice.

The first call stands, because a silently replaced program is a change nobody can see. A program that then fails cancels its hand-over along with everything else it decided, and the turn is an ordinary error turn instead. Chains are bounded: one hand-over per turn, and the program handed over does the work.

Throws `ToolError`: `ToolErrorCode.REFUSED` for a second hand-over in one turn, and `ToolErrorCode.INVALID_ARGUMENT` for a blank source.

parameters.name: source
parameters.doc: The program to run in place of this one, as Java statements. It may not be blank.

functions.name: source
functions.brief: Fetch this program's source, which is `Programs.get(int)` on the turn it ran.
functions.detail:
Returns: the source of the program that ran on this turn

Throws `ToolError`: `ToolErrorCode.NOT_FOUND` when the library has dropped it.

functions.name: finish
functions.brief: End the session, reporting what was done in a sentence or two.
functions.detail: The one thing that ends a working agent's session. It is best called last, once the tools have confirmed the work is really done.

parameters.name: summary
parameters.doc: What was done, in a sentence or two.

functions.name: approve
functions.brief: Accept the work under review: it meets every completion criterion and stays in scope.
functions.detail: This ends a reviewing agent's session, and is best called once the change has actually been read.

functions.name: requestChanges
functions.brief: Reject the work under review, listing every change it needs before it can be accepted.
functions.detail:
This ends a reviewing agent's session. Each item says what is wrong and what to change.

Throws `ToolError`: `ToolErrorCode.INVALID_ARGUMENT` when the list is empty.

parameters.name: items
parameters.doc: Every change the work needs before it can be accepted, one per entry: what is wrong, and what to change. The list may not be empty.

types.detail: The whole documentation of a function — every shape it may be called in, what to put in each argument, and the types it names — is a view rather than a value, opened with `Views.openDocsView`.

members.brief: The failure class, so a catch site branches on a value rather than on prose.

types.name: ToolErrorCode
types.declaration: enum ToolErrorCode { INVALID_ARGUMENT, NOT_FOUND, CONFLICT, REFUSED, UNAVAILABLE, LIMIT_EXCEEDED, IO_ERROR, OTHER }
types.brief: Why a gg call failed, as a value a catch site branches on rather than prose it has to match.
types.detail: The set is gg's and is closed. A code this SDK has no constant for arrives as `OTHER` rather than as a crash, because a program that cannot name a failure can still handle it.

members.name: INVALID_ARGUMENT
members.brief: The arguments were malformed, ill-typed, or out of range.
members.detail: A path that climbs out of the workspace and an agent name this run does not declare are both this.

members.name: NOT_FOUND
members.brief: The named thing does not exist.
members.detail: A file, a skill, a memory, a task, an epic, an issue, a subagent, a stored program, or a documentation entry.

members.name: CONFLICT
members.brief: Well-formed, but in conflict with the current state.
members.detail: An ambiguous edit, a dependency cycle, a duplicate id, a subagent that has already returned.

members.name: REFUSED
members.brief: gg refused the call on a rule about the session's state.
members.detail: A compaction in flight that this call is not the one it asked for, a memory call while memories are read-only, a second ending or hand-over in one turn, or a hook that blocked it. A ceiling that was hit is `LIMIT_EXCEEDED` rather than this.

members.name: UNAVAILABLE
members.brief: The call exists, and this run's capability set does not offer it.

members.name: LIMIT_EXCEEDED
members.brief: A gg-side ceiling was hit.
members.detail: A shell timeout, a store cap, the delegation depth cap, or the run's wall-clock budget.

members.name: IO_ERROR
members.brief: The underlying I/O or process failed.

members.name: OTHER
members.brief: The failure was not classified.
members.detail: Reserved for outcomes raised outside a tool implementation; nothing in this SDK produces one.

types.name: TaskPatch
types.brief: The fields a task revision changes, built a call at a time.
types.detail:
A revision has to carry at least one field, and a field it never names is left alone. The description is a three-way edit, which is why it has two methods rather than one: never naming it keeps what is there, `description` replaces it, and `clearDescription` empties it.

```java
Tasks.updateTask("parse", new Tasks.TaskPatch().status(Tasks.TaskStatus.DONE));
```

members.name: title(String title)
members.brief: Replace the task's title.

members.name: description(String description)
members.brief: Replace the task's description.

members.name: clearDescription()
members.brief: Clear the task's description, leaving it with none.

members.name: status(Tasks.TaskStatus status)
members.brief: Move the task to another status.

types.detail: The taxonomy is closed at three deliberately: everything on disk is a file, everything a program can compute is a string, and documentation is neither — gg holds it.
